status: conditional combinatorics and causal analysis; not a selected learner
value_lineage: C-15/P-29 requires contextual prediction; P-30 depends on C-13 fixed incoming capacity. Dependency does not confer authority.

source_eligibility.example: A context predicts alternatives B and C; B is then observed, followed by D.
source_eligibility.conditional_risk: Crediting readiness for C as though C had been observed can strengthen C-to-D in a rule that intends credit for observed context. This does not establish that all weak predictive activity is useless as history.
alternatives: Credit the independently established preceding contextual representation
Use graded preceding neural activity, distinguishing the role of weak readiness
source_eligibility.comparison: Compare later pre-input matching, retained legitimate alternatives, shared-fragment discrimination and contamination from unobserved branches. No winner array, causal noise labels or eligibility trace is selected.
source_eligibility.timing: If neural frames are finer than token events, the preceding frame need not be the preceding token. Define credit at the information boundary actually used; the two-frame buffer alone stores no arbitrary-length history.

local_operations.condition: Source ID already retained in the target set
local_operations.consequence: Weight adaptation needs no new endpoint slot; numerical update visibility is a separate issue.

local_operations.condition: Needed source absent, useful free slot present
local_operations.consequence: An independently defined structural-growth operation can assign it; scanning or adapting only existing edges cannot discover that endpoint.

local_operations.condition: Needed source absent and current set full
local_operations.consequence: Consider another context-compatible target, justified edge replacement, available larger set, or deferral. These change different semantics and none is selected.

local_operations.condition: Prediction wrong despite available source and slot
local_operations.consequence: Capacity alone does not repair target assignment, context discrimination, timing or effective gain.

assignment_condition.statement: With one set per participating target, interchangeable sets and no extra placement restrictions, sort positive live degrees d and available capacities c in descending order. A static fit exists iff count(d)<=count(c) and d[i]<=c[i] for every i.
assignment_condition.proof: Necessity: the i largest demands require i capacities at least d[i]. Sufficiency: assign the i-th largest demand to the i-th largest capacity.
assignment_condition.equivalent: For every integer demand threshold, the number of targets at or above it must not exceed the number of sets at or above it.
assignment_condition.limits: A feasibility statement, not a runtime sort, histogram, migration algorithm or guarantee of a free destination during online changes.

source_union.identity: d_i = size(union of retained source-ID sets for all associations assigned to target i); repeated source IDs need no additional slot under the one-weight-per-source/target reference.
source_union.assumptions: r independent uniform k-subsets of U possible source identities, with every chosen edge retained. No deletion, contextual selection bias or weight-threshold criterion; expectation, not a realized bound or measured training demand.
source_union.limits: A 60-cell subset example concerns repeated selection for the same target; it is not the full token encoder or a limit on global contexts. Fractional participation does not make a fractional endpoint-ID slot. Different weights for the same source/target conditioned on context would require separately justified semantics.

migration.invariant: Representation-only migration preserves effective weights and neural identity, not merely stored code bits.
migration.boundary: A capacity-class-dependent interpretation would make an unchanged graph change response on migration. H-24 places scaling in training; no per-row scale field, recoding scheme or class normalization is selected.

source_discovery_work.status: exact conditional probability and work arithmetic, not runtime performance
source_discovery_work.value_lineage: C-15/P-29 needs absent-source discovery; P-30 depends on fixed incoming storage. H-34/H-74 require demonstrated value before auxiliary structures.
assumptions: One target row of d distinct retained source IDs, unchanged during one successful proposal.
Independent proposals from a fixed probability distribution over a diagnostic universe of U IDs.
Reject represented IDs; accept the first absent ID. Positive absent probability is required.
Linear membership check in row order, stopping at the first equal ID or after d comparisons.
Weighted examples distribute total retained proposal mass uniformly over the d row positions.
U=614400 is an illustrative universe, not a selected self-edge, semantic eligibility or credit policy.
Excludes candidate-generation cost, activity reads, edge writes, migration and hardware effects.

identities.accepted_ID_probability: p_i/(1-m) for an absent i, where m=sum(retained p_i)
identities.limits: If m=1, no absent ID has positive proposal probability. Later accepted edges change m and the row.

non_adoptions: No rejection loop, hash table, bitmap, ordered row or auxiliary source index selected.
Low proposal rejection alone does not establish cheap membership checks or useful source selection.
Sampling source IDs without persistent absent-edge parameters does not inherit a Bayesian convergence guarantee.
